title: PosePackage
description: Canonical pose package v2: per-bone local rotations + root translation on a shared timestamp grid. Right-handed coordinates, +Y up, character faces +Z, meters/radians/seconds. Local transforms are relative to the parent bone; rest local rotations are identity [0,0,0,1] and non-root local translations are constant (see the rig manifest restLocal fields). Quaternion components are in [x,y,z,w] order and hemisphere-continuous so consumer slerp takes the short arc. Version 2 changes: quality checks are structured ({code, ok, label, value, limit, unit, worstTime}) and support events carry the side.

id.description: Artifact identity: hash of request fingerprint + action.definitionSHA256 + rig.manifestSHA256 + solver name/revision. The same request under a different definition, rig or solver yields a different id.

poseMode.description: Per-bone local transform relative to its parent bone. Unanimated bones inherit manifest restLocal; only 'root' carries a translation track.

parameters.description: Echo of the resolved action parameters; the artifact hash binds action.definitionSHA256, not this field. Bundled actions ship {} — the action id is the whole parameterization. Ad-hoc 'workshop-doc' packages carry {documentName, presentation}: documentName is the submitted document's display name, and presentation records display hints the trajectory itself cannot express — presentation.prop ('racket') marks that the document solved with grip constraints so a consumer may mount the prop (v2 carries no per-frame grip channel; the prop is either constantly present or absent), presentation.gripSide ('L') is the package-level constant mount side when the prop is left-handed ('R' stays absent — the document itself carries the solve-affecting copy), presentation.bevel (integer 1–8) is the package-level constant handle facet the palm rests on (absent means bevel 1, the canonical facet; the numbering is palm-relative, and the bevel only orients the prop — it is not a solve input), and presentation.loop mirrors the document's authored loop flag (consumers should treat loop:false as one-shot). Fields beyond these are per-action and not interpreted here.

definitionSHA256.description: Sorted-key canonical JSON hash of the fully resolved action definition.

fps.description: Output sample grid; the solver's internal dt is recorded separately in provenance when relevant.

timestamps.description: Action-relative seconds, strictly increasing, last entry exactly equal to duration — the single time truth. Uniform 1/fps grid; the final interval may be partial when duration×fps is non-integer.

values.description: Flattened [x,y,z] × timeline.count — the root bone's world-space position.

rotations.description: One entry per animated bone (identity throughout ⇒ omitted).

side.description: Foot side of a support-start/support-end event.

events.description: Named moments on the timeline. Support events name the foot in side and mark the boundary of one planted interval.

ok.description: True when the worst observed value is within limit (no tolerance).

value.description: Worst observed value over the motion; null when not applicable.

worstTime.description: Timeline second at which the worst value occurs.

quality.description: Measured per-check results. Template/rig/solver-specific measurements, not a claim of general biomechanical validity.

requestFingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the sorted-key canonical request body — what the client asked for. Unlike the artifact id it does not cover the definition, rig or solver version.
